Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 27-Dec-2024 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  FIRST SEMESTER B.Tech. (CSE STREAM) EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2024 / JANUARY 2025  
  SUBJECT: CHM 1072/CHM_1072 - APPLIED CHEMISTRY FOR ENGINEERS  
  (MAKEUP/REGULAR)  
  
  
  APPLIED CHEMISTRY FOR ENGINEERS [CHM 1072]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                    Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               i) What are the similarities and differences between lithium and sodium for battery applications?     (4)  
  ii) Describe the chemical reactions that occur in a lead-acid battery during charging and  
  overcharging.  
1B)               Explain the construction and working of the nickel metal hydride battery with the necessary diagram (4)  
  and chemical reactions. Give the advantages of nickel metal hydride battery.  
1C)               Write the advantages of solid polymeric electrolytes.                                                 (2)  
2A)               i) Discuss the mechanism of p-doping in conducting polymers by providing a specific example.          (4)  
  ii) Explain the relationship between polymer structure and its strength, and mention two factors that  
  influence the glass transition temperature  
2B)               i) Name the process used to form polyamides and provide a general scheme for this formation.          (4)  
  ii) Describe the preparation method and key applications of Nylon 6,6 in detail.  
2C)               Define Intrinsic Viscosity and state Mark-Houwink's equation. Explain each term in the equation and (2)  
  sketch a suitable graph illustrating the relationship between intrinsic viscosity and molecular weight.  
3A)               Give a reason for the following:                                                                      (4)  
  i) Individual metal components have higher conductivity than the alloy.  
  ii) Resistivity of the metal decreases initially with increasing pressure.  
  iii) Metals appear opaque to electromagnetic radiation within the visible region of the spectrum  
  iv) Laser is a special application of luminescence  
3B)               Write a note on the following:                                                                        (4)  
  i) Biosensors  
  ii) Electrochemical sensor  
3C)               Describe the optical phenomena exhibited by non-metals.                                               (2)  
4A)               i) Differentiate between recycling economy and circular economy.                                      (4)  
  ii) Explain how repair and refurbishment can reduce electronic waste.  
  iii) List any two potential health effects of PFAS exposure.  
  (1+2+1 = 4 marks)  
4B)               i) Elaborate on any two steps to be followed while rethinking product design for disassembly and      (4)  
  repairability.  
  ii) Describe water pollution through improper e-waste disposal.  
  (2+2 = 4 marks)  
4C)               What are fuel cells? How do they differ from conventional galvanic cells?                             (2)  
5A)               i) Classify biodegradable polymers, mention any two advantages and applications.                      (4)  
  ii) Discuss nanomaterials based on origin with examples.

(3+1 = 4 marks)  
5B)   i) Explain in detail the preparation of nanomaterials by sol-gel method.   (4)  
  ii) Explain the role of organic layers in the basic structure of OLED's.  
  (3+1 = 4 marks)  
5C)   Explain the principle of flame photometry.                                 (2)
